newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Aug crude imports jump 19 pct yr/yr - MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan Aug crude imports jump 19 pct yr/yr - MITI.

text.p: Japan imported 25.16 million kilolitres (kl) of crude oil in August, up 19 percent from the same period a year earlier and up 39.4 percent from July, the trade ministry said on Thursday.
A Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) official told reporters there was no specific reason for the sharp rise in August imports.
"Fluctuations in imports are mostly due to crude oil shipment schedules," the MITI official said.
The sharp increase in August imports offsets the drop in July imports, he said.
Japan, which relies heavily on the Middle East for its crude oil, imported 19.61 million kl from that area, which accounted for 77.9 percent of total August imports, MITI said.

The United Arab Emirates, which produces crude grades such as Dubai and Murban, was the top source of crude oil for the 36th straight month, MITI said. Imports from the UAE accounted for 6.6 million kilolitres, or 30.3 percent of total imports.
Saudi Arabia was the second largest supplier to Japan with imports reaching 5.04 million kl, followed by Iranian crude imports of 2.1 million kl.
In August, the first ever Alaskan crude imports of 206,354 kl reached Japan, MITI said.
Japanese refiners processed 21.68 million kl of crude in August, up 4.7 percent from the same period a year earlier, marking a year-on-year rise for the fourth consecutive month.

Refinery operating rates were at 83.1 percent, up from 80.1 percent a year earlier. Utilisation rates generally rise towards the end of the year as refiners build kerosene stocks for the winter months.
The amount of crude used for direct burning by electricity utilities fell 2.6 percent to 1.76 million kl from a year earlier, but rose 14.1 percent from July, MITI said.
